title: Understanding Zero-One Loss
text: Zero-one loss is a type of loss function used in classification problems. It counts the number of incorrect predictions made by the model. Unlike cross-entropy loss, which is continuous and differentiable, zero-one loss is discrete and non-differentiable.

title: Parameters in Zero-One Loss
text: In the context of zero-one loss, the parameters beta and T are adjusted to minimize the number of incorrect predictions. This is different from cross-entropy loss, where only beta is adjusted to minimize the loss.

title: Comparing Loss Functions
text: Consider how zero-one loss and cross-entropy loss differ in terms of their dependency on beta and T. Which loss function depends on both parameters?

title: Minimizing Zero-One Loss
text: To minimize zero-one loss, both beta and T need to be optimized. This is because zero-one loss is a function of both parameters, unlike cross-entropy loss, which only depends on beta.
